newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady, weak tone-dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady, weak tone-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hogs sold early Wednesday steady with a weak tone as packer demand remained light in the face of unprofitable operating margins, livestock dealers said.

Slaughter cutbacks as much as one to two hours per shift remained in effect at many plants, they said. Cutbacks started on Monday as packers scaled back in an attempt to improve margins. The light demand offset potential support from ongoing light marketings, sources said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $54.00-$55.50 per cwt in the country and $56.00-$56.50 at plants.
Illinois hogs sold steady at $54.50 to $55.50 in the country and $56.00 at plants.

Hogs in Indiana sold steady at $54.50 to $55.00 in the country and $56.00 to $56.75 at plants. Prices in Illinois and Indiana were seen holding steady amid strong demand from IBP Inc hog buyers looking to fill inventories for the newly opened second shift in Logansport, Ind.
Ohio hogs sold steady at $51.50 to $52.50 in the country and $53.00 to $54.00 at plants.
Marketings were light in Illinois, Indiana and Ohio as farmers increased fieldwork, curbing time to market hogs.
